brief.intro: Landscape works turn a graded site into finished external areas — hard landscape (paving, kerbs, walls, steps, water features, furniture) and soft landscape (topsoil, planting, lawns and irrigation). New to this type? There is almost no building MEP here; the programme is driven by earthworks and grading first, buried drainage and irrigation next, then hardscape, then planting followed by an establishment / maintenance period before handover. It is weather- and season-sensitive, and finished areas must be protected from the trades that follow.

scope.name: Setting out & grading
scope.desc: Survey, cut/fill to design levels, and formation of falls to drainage.

scope.name: Drainage & sub-base
scope.desc: Land drainage, sub-surface drainage and compacted sub-base under paving.

scope.name: Irrigation mains & first fix
scope.desc: Buried irrigation mains, sleeves and control wiring laid before paving.

scope.name: Hardscape
scope.desc: Paving, kerbs, retaining and feature walls, steps and edge restraints.

scope.name: Water features & pumps
scope.desc: Pools, fountains and their pumps, plant and treatment.

scope.name: Site electrical & lighting
scope.desc: Feature and pathway lighting, irrigation controllers and power to features.

scope.name: Soil placement & preparation
scope.desc: Topsoil placement, grading, amelioration and preparation of planting beds.

scope.name: Planting
scope.desc: Trees, shrubs, groundcover and lawns / turf or seeding.

scope.name: Site furniture & signage
scope.desc: Benches, bins, bollards, play/sport equipment and signage.

scope.name: Establishment / maintenance
scope.desc: The care period after planting until the landscape is accepted and handed over.

glossary.plain: the built, paved external elements — paving, walls, steps, features.
the living parts — soil, planting, lawns and trees.
the compacted stone layer that supports paving.
the buried pipes and sleeves laid before paving goes down.
the fertile upper soil for planting vs the layer beneath.
the post-planting care time until the plants take and it is handed over.
a barrier that stops roots damaging paving or services.

must_get_right: Grading and drainage come first — everything else sits on correct levels and falls.
Buried services and irrigation first-fix must go in before paving; retrofitting under paving is costly.
Planting is season-dependent — align the softscape window with the right season, or hold it.
Programme the establishment / maintenance period, and protect finished areas from following trades.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network in Primavera P6 developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress; calculated by F9 with total float kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: A 6-day site week, with planting scheduled inside the correct planting season and an explicit weather allowance for wet/hot periods. The establishment period runs on a maintenance calendar after practical completion of planting.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs grading → drainage & buried services → irrigation first fix → hardscape → topsoil & planting → establishment → handover. Late-season planting or a missed weather window, not the hardscape, most often governs the finish.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Formation levels are handed over correct and on time by earlier packages; topsoil and specified plant stock are available in the required season; water supply for irrigation and establishment is available; and finished areas are protected by others.

sections.heading: Key quantities & seasonal windows
sections.body: The programme is quantity- and season-driven rather than long-lead-equipment driven — the main drivers are tracked as quantities and windows:

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Working over/around finished areas needs protection; irrigation water supply and disposal; and coordination with building trades still completing adjacent works are the main constraints.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: weather delay to earthworks and planting, plant-establishment failure (replacement in the defect period), and damage to finished landscape by following trades. Contingency is held before the planting window and before handover.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1–2 to the client, controlled at Level 3, expanded to a Level 4–5 field lookahead — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
